audit.retention.law: Readings and the audit trail stay on the fast path for {{hot}} months, then move to archive storage. Everything is kept for {{years}} years in total and nothing older is deleted before that.
audit.retention.link: Data retention — has it ever run? →
audit.retention.neverManual: There is no way to start, skip or bring forward a retention run from this product, by design. It runs {{schedule}}.
audit.retention.neverRan: has never been archived — the retention job has not run on this deployment.
audit.retention.noOp: This run found nothing old enough to move. That is a normal outcome and is recorded on purpose.
audit.retention.noRuns: No retention run has ever been recorded on this deployment. Nothing has been archived and nothing has been deleted.
audit.retention.notOffSite: Archived means moved off the fast path, counted and checksummed, and still readable here. It does NOT yet mean copied off this database: no off-site destination is configured, so every run records that it shipped nothing.

billing.action.runBillsBlocked: The billing run wizard is its own screen and there is no endpoint to start a run yet.
billing.arrives.oneTime: A one-time bill charges a single account outside the cycle. It uses the same run in single-account mode, and arrives with it.
billing.arrives.run: Running a billing run is a guided screen of its own: pick the cycle, check what was found, review the customers, see the totals, sign off, and send the bills out. It arrives with the billing run work.
billing.bill.action.correctDraft: A draft is not corrected — it is re-run. Corrections apply to bills the customer has received.
billing.bill.action.openNewTab: Open it in a new tab ↗
billing.bill.action.reprintChecking: Checking whether a printable copy exists.
billing.bill.action.reprintDraft: A draft has not been issued, so there is no saved copy to print.
billing.bill.action.reprintNoDocument: No saved copy was recorded for this bill, so there is nothing to print.
billing.bill.action.voidAlready: This bill is already canceled. Canceling never deletes it, so the record stays exactly as it is.
billing.bill.action.voidBlocked: Before a bill is canceled you must be shown, in plain words, what it will do: which entries reverse, how the balance changes, whether a payment has to be reversed first and whether an approval is needed. The server works that out, and the endpoint that does it has not been built.
billing.bill.action.voidDraft: A draft is not canceled — it is simply not issued.
billing.bill.approve.title: Approve this bill?
billing.bill.arrives.delivery: This deployment cannot say where this bill was sent: the part of the product that holds the delivery queue is not answering. Nothing is shown rather than an empty list, because an empty list would read as “this bill was never sent”.
billing.bill.authorityAbsentWhy: The tax is recorded on this line. The authority's name could not be read.
billing.bill.breakdownAbsentWhy: This server sends no per-service totals. The charges are on Charges.
billing.bill.byServiceAbsentWhy: The server sent no per-service breakdown for this bill.
billing.bill.byServiceBillLevel: Charged to the bill, not to a service
billing.bill.byServiceDoesNotTieOut: These lines add up to {{lines}} and the bill says {{bill}}. Nothing here changes either figure.
billing.bill.byServiceMinimumMisfiled: The minimum-bill top-up sits here rather than under its own service. The bill's total is unaffected — only this heading is wrong.
billing.bill.byServiceNone: No charge on this bill belongs to a service.
billing.bill.byServiceTiesOut: These add up to the bill's total.
billing.bill.cancelDraft.consequence: The draft is deleted. Its number is not reused.
billing.bill.cancelDraft.title: Cancel this draft?
billing.bill.chain.isLatest: Nothing has replaced it, and no credit note or replacement bill is recorded against it.
billing.bill.chain.openCurrent: Open {{billNo}}, the bill that counts now →
billing.bill.chain.standingUnknown: We could not check whether this is the current bill
billing.bill.chain.supersededWhy: This bill stays exactly as the customer received it. A replacement bill was issued and it is the one that counts.
billing.bill.correctAgainNote: A further correction applies to the replacement bill, not to this one.
billing.bill.creditNotesNone: No credit note is recorded against this bill.
billing.bill.deliveryEmpty: Nothing has been queued for this bill. Bills join the queue when they are issued, so a draft has no delivery history yet.
billing.bill.deliveryQueuedOnly: Every bill also goes on paper.
billing.bill.documentNotStampedWhy: A complete copy of the bill is frozen the moment it is issued, and every re-print comes from that copy. A draft has not been issued, so there is nothing to print.
billing.bill.dueHint: Late-payment terms are the utility's own words, printed in the bill message. Nothing here writes them.
billing.bill.failedTitle: This bill could not be opened
billing.bill.field.documentTiesOut: Saved bill matches its charge lines
billing.bill.field.postingBalanced: Posted amounts add up to the amount owed
billing.bill.glAbsentWhy: Every line records the accounting code it posted to at the moment the bill was issued. This line carries none.
billing.bill.howTheyHearAbsentWhy: The account this bill belongs to could not be read, so where it would go is not shown.
billing.bill.integrityFigures: Saved bill: {{payload}} over {{payloadLines}} line(s). Charge lines: {{rows}} over {{rowLines}} line(s).
billing.bill.integrityNo: No — these do not match. Do not treat this bill as settled until someone has looked at it.
billing.bill.linesEmpty: This bill has no charge lines, which should not happen — a bill with no lines has nothing to pay.
billing.bill.notFound: We could not read this bill. Either it does not exist for this utility, or the endpoint that reads a single bill has not been built yet — the two answer the same way, so neither is claimed over the other.
billing.bill.panel.adjustmentsHint: An adjustment is its own row. An issued bill is never edited.
billing.bill.panel.chainHint: Correcting a bill never changes it. The original stays exactly as the customer received it, and the correction is a credit note and, where one is needed, a replacement bill.
billing.bill.panel.documentHint: The bill a customer received is re-printed exactly as it was sent, from the copy saved when it was issued. A re-print six months later shows July's name and address, not today's.
billing.bill.panel.integrityHint: Two things are checked on every bill you open: the saved copy of the bill matches the charge lines behind it, and the amounts posted to the books add up to what the customer owes. Both are shown so a mismatch cannot sit here unnoticed.
billing.bill.panel.linesHint: The accounting code on each line is the one that was recorded when the bill was issued. Changing the mapping later never changes an old bill.
billing.bill.panel.originHint: The service date decides which rates priced this bill. It is never today's rates.
billing.bill.panel.pinHint: The template decides how the bill looks; the saved bill data decides what it says. They are versioned separately, so changing a template never changes an old bill.
billing.bill.panel.summaryHint: These four are as at issue. Owed today is the live balance.
billing.bill.panel.taxesHint: A tax is charged on the bill, not on one service. Nothing records which service a tax belongs to.
billing.bill.panel.usageHint: This period comes from the bill. The average is the account's, over twelve months.
billing.bill.pastDueUnknownWhy: Whether this bill is past due was not worked out for this bill.
billing.bill.pastDueYes: Yes — the due date has passed and it is unpaid
billing.bill.summary.owedTodayWhy: The account's open position has not answered yet.
billing.bill.summary.paymentsCreditsWhy: Payments and credits received before this bill are the payments module's record, saved onto the bill when it was issued.
billing.bill.summary.previousBalanceWhy: The balance carried forward is the utility's ledger position on the day the bill was issued. It is saved onto the bill at that moment, and nothing here recalculates it.
billing.bill.summaryAbsentWhy: Every bill saves its previous balance, payments received and current charges the day it is issued. This bill carries none, which is a fact about the bill — it is not a zero.
billing.bill.taxesNoAuthoritySubtotal: A total per authority is not available yet. Only the whole bill's tax is shown.
billing.bill.taxesTieOut: These add up to the tax.
billing.bill.unitMissingWhy: A quantity is never shown without the unit it was measured in. This line carries a number and no unit, which is a fault in the record rather than something to guess at.
billing.bill.usage.readAbsentWhy: The saved bill records whether a meter was read, never which one.
billing.bill.usageNoneWhy: Every charge on this bill is a fixed one.
billing.bills.awaits.endpoint: The bill tables landed with no way to read them. Until the list endpoint is built this table can show nothing — and an empty table would read as “this utility has never billed anyone”, which is a different statement. Nothing else on this screen changes when it arrives.
billing.bills.awaits.endpointTitle: Waiting on the bills read endpoint

customers.accounts.arrives.disconnects: This will hold the reminder ladder, the protections that freeze it — a medical certificate, a payment plan, a weather moratorium — the cut itself and the reconnection. Nothing is recorded here yet, and how the ladder behaves once an account has closed is still being decided.
customers.accounts.arrives.moveIns: Move-ins will be listed here from the day a new occupant is booked in to the day their account opens. The move-in you can run today is on the unit's own page; this worklist, and the ability to park one part-way and come back to it, arrive later.
customers.accounts.arrives.moveOuts: Move-outs will be listed here from the closing read to the final bill. The move-out you can run today is on the account's own page; this worklist arrives later, and it waits on a decision about what happens to money a customer still owes once their account has closed.
customers.accounts.arrives.newConnects: New connects will follow a build from the first inquiry through to activated services and open accounts. Nothing is recorded here yet. The connection charges go to the owner's own account, created with the build.
customers.accounts.arrives.requests: This is where a customer's application to start, move or stop service will be tracked, from the moment it arrives to the moment it becomes an account. Nothing is recorded here yet: the request itself is still being designed, including which documents a utility must hold on file before one can be approved.
customers.accounts.arrives.requestsBuilt: Service requests are built and live on their own screen — the list, each request's detail, the capture form and the document checklist. Showing that list inside this tab is still to come; the button takes you straight to it.
customers.accounts.arrives.transfers: A transfer is one job: the same customer, a new address, with the deposit carried across instead of refunded and collected again. It is kept out of Move-ins and Move-outs on purpose, so one job is never counted twice. Nothing is recorded here yet.
customers.accounts.awaits.billing: The Aging column is worked out from what each account owed when it was migrated across, so an account whose debt comes from a bill we issued shows a dash rather than a band. The Past due 60+ tile is left uncounted for the same reason: a count from migrated balances alone would miss those accounts and read lower than the truth.
customers.accounts.awaits.other: There is no plan column and no plan filter: the plan recorded against an account has no table yet, and a unit's plan is not the same thing. CSV export has no accounts route, and autopay is recorded here but nothing collects on it in this version.

finance.gap.a_statement_names_one_accoun: A statement opens on one account.
finance.gap.active_connection_classes_ar: This figure counts active, marked-for-disconnect and vacation-hold accounts together. Accounts publishes one total that also includes pending and closed ones, so showing that total here would be a wrong number rather than a rough one.
finance.gap.activity_feed_has_no_event_r: Nothing in this product yet records bill runs, payments and imports as one dated stream, so there is no activity to list. An empty list here would read as “nothing happened today”.
finance.gap.aging_buckets_need_invoice_d: Ledger lines carry no due date. The bands cannot be split.
finance.gap.aging_does_not_foot_to_the_a: These bands do not add up to the receivable in the books. That difference is a real one to investigate — this report never adjusts itself to hide it.
finance.gap.ar_control_total_not_publish: The ledger's receivable total could not be read, so this report cannot say whether it agrees with the books.
finance.gap.balance_moved_to_owner_witho: Some moved balances have no bill.
finance.gap.billing_cycle_window_is_not_: Reporting over a whole billing cycle is not offered. Every window you can pick states the exact dates it covers.
finance.gap.bills_shared_against_what_th: Budget bills shared by amount asked.
finance.gap.bills_shared_without_class_o: Some part-paid bills shared by amount.
finance.gap.cash_window_holds_more_than_: Payments are in several currencies. No total can be shown.
finance.gap.charge_code_references_are_n: We cannot see which charge codes point at an account, so no account is ever deleted on that evidence.
finance.gap.customer_register_could_not_: The customer register could not be read at all, so this side is shown as unknown rather than as nothing. A register nobody could open and a register holding nothing are different facts.
finance.gap.deposit_register_is_never_wr: Nothing in this product writes the customer deposit register, so the books and the register are kept by different paths. A difference here means the register is not being maintained — not that the books are wrong.
finance.gap.dso_needs_twelve_months_of_b: This measure needs twelve months. The books hold fewer.
finance.gap.failed_payment_count_is_not_: Payments publishes the fifty most recent failed payments for its own screen, not a count of all of them. On a utility with more than fifty this tile would say fifty and be wrong.
finance.gap.gl_mapping_bulk_write_is_not: There is no single Save for the whole map. Each half is saved where it belongs: a role here, a service's revenue account on Settings → Services.
finance.gap.imported_opening_buckets_are: Balances brought in from your old system are not in these bands: nothing stores them yet, so a utility that migrated will see less here than it is owed.
finance.gap.issued_bill_without_an_issue: Some issued bills carry no issue date and cannot be placed in a period, so they are left out of this report rather than moved into it.
finance.gap.journal_number_series_is_not: This entry has no JE number: no numbering series for journal entries has been set up on this utility. The entry is in the books either way.
finance.gap.late_fee_revenue_has_no_desi: Nothing marks the late-fee account. This figure cannot be summed.
finance.gap.manual_je_role_gate_is_a_rea: Who may post a manual entry was read from the ruling on reversals — System Admin and Billing Clerk. It has not been ruled for this screen specifically.
finance.gap.no_account_carries_the_accou: No account in this chart is marked as the receivables account, so there is no receivable to report on. One edit to the chart of accounts fixes it.
finance.gap.no_account_carries_the_depos: No account in this chart is marked as the customer deposit account, so deposits taken have nowhere to be held in the books and there is nothing to compare.
finance.gap.open_bill_without_a_due_date: Some unpaid bills carry no due date, so they cannot be aged. Their amount is in each account's total and in none of the bands.
finance.gap.owner_books_not_published: The books could not be read.
finance.gap.owner_summary_differs_from_t: The total differs from the books.
finance.gap.pending_approval_count_is_no: Adjustments awaiting approval are not posted. The books cannot count them.
finance.gap.per_authority_remitting_basi: No remitting basis is chosen. Set it in Settings → Configure.
finance.gap.per_service_tax_and_collecte: Tax is not held per service. Cash is not linked to bills.
finance.gap.posted_entries_without_a_je_: Journal numbering is not set up.
finance.gap.premises_and_unit_dimensions: No line here carries a premises. Older entries never will.
finance.gap.premises_filter_is_not_offer: This report does not accept a premises filter. The ledger lines carry the dimension; the filter itself has not been built, and a control that filtered nothing would make the report look filtered.
finance.gap.receivable_holds_more_than_o: More than one currency is owed, so the bands cannot be added into a single total.
finance.gap.receivables_by_service_does_: Rows do not match the books. The report never adjusts itself.
finance.gap.register_window_holds_more_t: This range holds bills in more than one currency, so there is no single total to show.
finance.gap.repost_draft_is_not_persiste: The corrected copy is not saved yet. Check the figures and press Save draft — closing this now loses nothing but the copy.
finance.gap.revenue_window_holds_more_th: This range holds revenue in more than one currency, so the footer cannot be added up.
finance.gap.service_gl_attributes_seam_i: The service list could not be reached, so this section says nothing rather than saying nothing is mapped.
finance.gap.some_documents_carry_no_prin: A refund carries no printed number. Its Reference stays empty.
finance.gap.some_money_in_this_period_ca: Some of this period's activity carries no premises, so the table does not add up to the period total. The two unattributed figures below show how much.
finance.gap.tax_authority_references_are: We cannot see which tax authorities point at an account, so no account is ever deleted on that evidence.
finance.gap.tax_outstanding_is_the_bille: Outstanding tax is measured as what was billed less what was remitted. An authority you file on a cash basis is compared here on the billed basis instead.
finance.gap.the_stored_counts_blob_disag: Counts differ from the stored summary.
finance.gap.title: What is missing
finance.gap.unbilled_read_count_is_not_p: Meter Reads holds every reading but publishes no count of the ones still waiting to be billed. Counting them here would create a second counter of the same fact, and two counters eventually disagree.
finance.gap.unknown: The books will not state this.
finance.gap.which_bill_a_payment_met_is_: Payments are not linked to bills. This percentage cannot be worked out.
finance.gap.written_off_ytd_window_was_n: This page reads one period only. No year total was requested.

workflow.accounts.blurb: Upload the account file. Nothing is written until you commit at stage four.
workflow.accounts.next: Accounts attach to units that already exist — import premises and units first. Opening balances arrive as four aged bands, so aging is right from day one.
workflow.accounts.rollback: Rolling back closes every account this run created and removes its opening balances. An account that has already been billed is kept and reported — an issued bill cannot be unmade. A run that posted opening balances cannot be rolled back at all.
workflow.assets_devices.blurb: Upload the device file. A device seats on its premises' unit; nothing is written until stage four.
workflow.assets_devices.next: Devices with a test frequency join the lifecycle calendar — review the derived next-test dates.
workflow.assets_devices.rollback: Rolling back closes the assignment on every device this run created and returns it to Inventory. A device is kept and reported if it already carries reads, or if it has been retired since the load. Nothing is deleted.
workflow.assets_meters.blurb: Upload the meter file. Nothing is written until you commit at stage four.
workflow.assets_meters.next: Meters tag to their units as they load — a blank unit goes to inventory, ready to assign later.
workflow.assets_meters.rollback: Rolling back closes the assignment on every meter this run created and returns it to Inventory. A meter is kept and reported if it already carries reads, or if it has been retired since the load. Nothing is deleted.
workflow.assets_submeters.blurb: Upload the sub-meter file. Every sub-meter names its master; nothing is written until stage four.
workflow.assets_submeters.next: Sub-meters bill their own unit under their master — review the allocation shares from the registry.
workflow.assets_submeters.rollback: Rolling back closes the assignment on every sub-meter this run created and returns it to Inventory. A sub-meter is kept and reported if it already carries reads, or if it has been retired since the load. Nothing is deleted.

workflow.parts.blurb: Upload your parts list. Nothing is written until you commit at stage four.
workflow.parts.insertConsequence: A row naming a record already on file is REJECTED: it does not load, and nothing about that record changes. Fix the file or come back as Insert & update. Every other row is created.
workflow.parts.next: Parts stand on their own — nothing has to be loaded first. A category has to be one already on your register; leave the cell empty and the part loads without one.
workflow.parts.rollback: Rolling back removes every part this run added. A part that has already been issued to a job is kept and switched off instead — deleting it would take the materials record of that job with it.
workflow.payments.blurb: Upload the payment file. Nothing is written until commit.
workflow.payments.next: These payments join the payments list. Each one names its run.
workflow.payments.rollback: A posted payment cannot be unwritten. Discard the batch before you commit.
workflow.premises.blurb: One row per premises. Units and meters are separate imports.
workflow.premises.next: Units are next. Import them from the Units tab.
workflow.premises.rollback: Rolling back deactivates every premise this run created. A premise is kept and reported if any unit on it now has an active account. Nothing is deleted.
workflow.promise: Five stages · nothing is written until you commit at stage four.
workflow.reads.blurb: Upload the reading file, or type the readings in. Nothing is written until you commit at stage four.
workflow.reads.next: Committed readings can be billed. A reading that turns out to be wrong is corrected by a new reading that supersedes it — the original stays on the record.
workflow.reads.rollback: A posted read batch cannot be rolled back. Every reading it committed is permanent, and a wrong one is corrected by uploading the right one — which supersedes it and keeps both on the record. Cancel before you post to discard the batch instead.
workflow.reads.validateBlurb: Errors block the load. Warnings do not.
